_comment: Read at compile time, so the config can never silently drift: Rust reads it in `src-tauri/build.rs` (which re-emits environment variables for `src-tauri/src/lib.rs` to read via `env!`), and `src/main.tsx` imports the background-service pair, the launcher base URL and the Authorization app base URL. Change the values here and rebuild.
_host_app_client_scopes_comment: The scopes the host app's OAuth client may be granted: the authorization server seeds its allowed_scopes from this. Not the Owner's authority, which authorization-server-rust defines as OWNER_SCOPES.
_wildflower_host_app_client_id_comment: The `client_id` of the Wildflower host app's OAuth client. authorization-server-rust seeds the client row under this id; its `WILDFLOWER_HOST_APP_CLIENT_ID` const is the standalone/test fallback only.
_launcher_base_url_comment: The hosted launcher (`apps/launcher/launcher-web`'s `main-web` build) the host links browsers to — see `wildflowerhealthio_shared_structures::launcher`. Release builds use `launcher_base_url` (held to branding-core's `sectionUrl('launcher')` by `apps/launcher/launcher-web/src/launcher-address.test.ts`); debug builds use the `main-web` dev server on `dev-app-ports.json`'s `launcher-dev` port, which `src-tauri/build.rs` reads. `launcher_base_url` is also the launcher a new server gets, in every build: the host gives it to each server it adds (Rust, re-emitted by `src-tauri/build.rs`), and the base's server page offers Reset to default while a server's launcher differs from it (TS, imported by `src/main.tsx`).
_authorization_app_base_url_comment: The hosted Wildflower Authorization app, where the Owner manages what each server has authorized — see `wildflowerhealthio_shared_structures::authorization_app`. Every build gives it to each server it runs (Rust, re-emitted by `src-tauri/build.rs`), which advertises it, pointed back at itself, as its SMART discovery's `management_endpoint`. It is also the Authorization app a new server gets, which the server card's Authorization opens: the host gives it to each server it adds (Rust), and the base's server page offers Reset to default while a server's Authorization app differs from it (TS, imported by `src/main.tsx`).
_background_service_comment: How the background service starts the Wildflower server: the text of Android's persistent foreground-service notification, and its Android foreground-service type. The host starts the service with these (Rust, re-emitted by `src-tauri/build.rs`), and the Tauri entry hands the same pair to the plugin's `configureRecovery` for the restarts the plugin makes itself (TS, imported by `src/main.tsx`). The type must also be in `tauri.conf.json`'s `androidForegroundServiceTypes` and be the one the Android manifest narrows the plugin's service to; host tests hold both to this value.
